chapter_theme: A single song at Kodumbalur (கொடும்பாளூர், கொடும்பை in the text): a plea to leave the clamour of sects and arguments and know the knowledge that cannot be pointed to, with praise of Murugan as the merchant riding the peacock.

951.reading: The poet asks whether, leaving attachment to the countless arts of argument, the rites and quarrels of the six sects who divide and clamour, and the learning of scholars bound to this Kali age, he can know the knowledge that cannot be pointed to, abide a little in it, and receive the word of grace. The praise names Murugan the chest embraced by the young green creeper of the Kuravar called killers, the one before whom the cruel Krauncha and the demon perished while the sea, the encircling mountains and the ten directions shook, and the merchant (செட்டி) who rides the golden horse that is the peacock, at Kodumbai.
951.nuance: குறியாத அறிவை அறிந்து: the knowledge sought is one without a mark or sign, set against தர்க்கப் பலகலை, the arts of disputation. The epithet செட்டி, the merchant, recalls the story of Murugan coming as a trader; the text names only the title and the peacock as his horse. அரவியிடம் தப்பி is obscure.

source_issues: Chapter heading spells the town கொடும்பாளுர் for கொடும்பாளூர்.

links.note: The song asks to leave the arts of disputation (தர்க்கப் பலகலை) and the quarrels of the six sects and know the knowledge that has no mark (குறியாத அறிவை அறிந்து). Tirumanthiram 2517 says the one who conquers the senses ends dispute quickly (பிணக்கறுவந்து) and knows the Pure One as one. Both make the end of argument the condition of the knowing.
